articleTitle: Machine learning based solar energy forecasting and wind-solar based hybrid grid arrangement at Patenga coastal area, Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Rapid developing country like Bangladesh will encounter a major problem in finding the sources for electricity generation as conventional sources of power are getting diminished due to shortage of fossil fuels. Renewable energy systems (RES) are the ultimate choice of future energy meet. RES like wind turbine generator (WTG) and solar photovoltaic generator (SPVG) are weather dependent and weather is a variable parameter. Prediction of weather in quick time is needed to study the nature of hybrid system. Present paper targets a potential location called Patenga, which is one of the coastal areas of Bangladesh. The annual average wind speed at 20 meter height is 7.48 ms<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and solar radiation is 5.85 kWh/m2/day. This paper will work on modelling of WTG, SPVG and analyzes the output of generators with the variation of weather as their respective source of energy. Weather of a particular day is extrapolated for solar irradiation using common machine learning approaches. The grid power response is also observed to find the overall response with RES of a day. All the simulations of the work are carried out by NEPLAN software.

articleTitle: IoT and Solar Based Smart Farming Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Bangladesh is a developing country which economy is heavily reliant on agriculture, thus the newly discovered technique will be efficient and useful in their efforts to grow crops productively. Various electronic devices/sensors, such as pH detectors, moisture detectors, thermometers, water level detectors, ultrasonic sensors, rain sensors, obstacle detectors, temperature and humidity sensors, and so on, are extremely difficult for farmers to use and incorporate individually into their farming operations. The proposed solar-powered microcontroller regulated model will operate above the electronic devices together at the same time. Analytical analysis was performed using FRITZING software. As a result, the included sensors sensed the output and delivered the input signal to the microcontroller, which precisely displayed the output on the display. In addition, this model uses solar technology to convert solar energy to electrical energy, which may then be stored in a DC battery for later use. The proposed system is an easily portable and user-friendly system that can take the farming process into a next level condition.

articleTitle: Realistic Behavior of Electrical Faults in $3-\Phi$ Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The main objective of this research work is to visualize realistic behaviour of electrical faults in induction motor. Modified dynamic induction motor model with electrical faults are proposed. Analytical analysis and simulation studies will be carried using MATLAB/Simulink R2021a software. The proposed model can be used to test fault in the three phase induction machines and fault diagnostic algorithms.

articleTitle: Simulation Research on Vehicle Handling and Stability Enhancement Based on PID Control Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Yaw stability control is a critical component of lateral and longitudinal dynamics, allowing for the improvement and evaluation of both vehicle handling and stability performance. A fourteen-degree-of-freedom model of a car with front steering is constructed in order to examine and analyze ways to improve the vehicle's yaw stability. The vehicle control system's feedback signal, which is the vehicle's yaw rate, is viewed as an input signal; we present a yaw moment control algorithm based on the PID controller. Two steering conditions are simulated in the simulations: a lane change maneuver and step steering. The simulation results indicate that the controlled vehicle's yaw rate follows a route close to the desired yaw rate target value; this indicates the success of both the controller utilized in this study and the mathematical equations developed.

articleTitle: Stockwell Transform & Data Mining based method for Fault detection and classification in PV Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In photovoltaic (PV) system, the output power is depending on the smooth operation of PV array. PV array may suffer from different fault condition due to open circuit, short circuit and partial shading condition. Fault is a abnormal condition that can cause hindrance to the smooth operation of PV system. Fault identification is major challenge to the design engineers to avoid power loss as well as damage to the PV system. Open circuit, short circuit and partial shading are most frequent faults that occur in PV array system. Many Researchers proposed fault diagnosis methods to recognize faults in PV array, majority failed in accurate and fast detection of faults. In this paper a novel method consists of Stockwell transform and machine learning based algorithm is used to detect and classify faults in PV array. The Necessary simulations and classification tasks are carried out in MATLAB Software.

articleTitle: A Load Shedding Methodology Using Monte Carlo Simulation in a Renewable Integrated Grid
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Voltage and frequency stability are the two most important factors to maintain the electricity supply interruption free. However, because of unprecedented events and disturbances, it often becomes very difficult to maintain uninterrupted supply of electricity. Load shedding is the final line of protection in the event of a major disturbance, preventing the system frequency from falling below a threshold value and the system from going into blackout. However, in some instances, the conventional Under Frequency Load Shedding (UFLS) approach may result in more deviation in frequency and load cut. The purpose of this study is to develop a load shedding method that enhances the frequency responsiveness of low inertia networks while maintaining acceptable voltage stability. The proposed strategy leverages the FVSI technique to apply a substantial share of load shedding to comparatively weaker buses considering voltage stability. Moreover, the load shedding amount has been limited by applying Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) approach. The developed strategy's performance is investigated in a modified IEEE 39 bus network. The simulations are run with two severe contingencies in mind: the loss of 560 MW generation and the loss of 832 MW generation. According to the findings of the research, the recommended load shedding mechanism helps to conserve adequate frequency response in all simulated scenarios. Furthermore, as compared to the traditional UFLS mechanism, the new approach results in reduced frequency fluctuation and load reduction.

articleTitle: A Critical Evaluation and Experimental Verification of Stator Inter-turn Short-Circuit Fault Detection and Diagnosis in $3-\Phi$ Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents a new model-based fault detection and diagnosis method for induction motors. The proposed strategy is based on generalized likelihood ratio (GLR), using statistical properties of residuals generated by extended Kalman filter. Under normal operation, the residuals follow Gaussian distribution, and they become non-Gaussian when a stator inter-turn short-circuit fault occurs in a motor. Unlike many existing methods that fail in realistic scenarios, the proposed method is robust to realistic conditions such as variable load, unbalanced input supply. To validate the proposed approach, computational programs are formulated and executed using MATLAB environment. Subsequently, experimental results are also included to validate the ability of the proposed strategy suitable for online fault detection and diagnosis.

articleTitle: High PV Generation Penetration on Power System Inertia: Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The growing integration of Photo-Voltaic (PV) system in the conventional power system has become a matter of concern due to its significant impact on the power system inertia. High penetration of inertia less PV system will replace conventional rotating mass turbine-based generators and therefore lowers the entire power system inertia which results in a negative impact on specially frequency and transient stability performances of power system. In this paper an overview of the impact of high PV penetration on conventional power system inertia has been presented followed by a brief discussion on the technologies to mitigate the challenges.

articleTitle: Solar Powered Automatic Irrigation System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: These research studies aim to develop a new automated irrigation method for agricultural land. Sprinklers and surface irrigation use roughly half of available water sources. Plants can get a more accurate amount of watering. Automatic Drip Irrigation is an extremely useful tool for precisely controlling soil moisture. Additionally, it assists in saving time, eliminating human error in adjusting available soil moisture levels, and optimizing their net yield. Farmers can mitigate runoff caused by overwatering saturated soils. The proposed model uses a microcontroller with AT Mega 328 Series microcontroller and sensors to detect moisture levels in the soil using an external hard-driven sensor for pumping water into the molds. When the controller gets this signal, it generates an output that drives the water pump ON or OFF. From Bangladesh's perspective, the suggested automated irrigation system is beneficial. Water distribution on fields or small gardens is easier and does not require constant operator management. This model is aimed for gardeners and farmers who lack time to water their plants. It also affects farmers who waste water when irrigating. Greenhouses, where manual supervision is rare, can employ the proposed model. The concept can be extended to fully automated gardens and farms.

articleTitle: Robust Backstepping Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Controller for a Grid-Tied Solar PV Unit
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This work offers a grid-connected solar photovoltaic (SPV) system with a fast power reaching law-based robust backstepping integrated terminal sliding mode controller. An output LCL filter is suggested instead of L filters for increasing the injected power quality. Despite the fact that an LCL filter can increase the quality of injected power, it will generate a resonance problem. As an external disturbance, the resonance problem is incorporated into the dynamical model. Following that, the proposed approach is used to generate the control rule, and the system's overall stability is ensured using the well-known Lyapunov theory. Finally, the simulation result, which was performed in MATLAB under various sun irradiances, is shown to demonstrate the use of the suggested method. To demonstrate the proposed controller's superiority over the present controller, the performance of injected grid current total harmonic distortions (THDs) is compared to that of existing controllers.

articleTitle: A MATLAB Simulated Design of an Energy-Efficient Solar-Powered Smart Kitchen
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Today, technology demands constant oversight. CO2 emissions from cooking, heating, and lighting account for 25% of total carbon emissions each year. Renewable energy can be remarkable in reducing pollution and the danger of human fatalities by contributing to energy generation. A kitchen design had presented in this study that optimizes solar power for cooking, water pumping, and other kitchen-related loads. Solar energy had harnessed as a power source through an MPPT controller. A solar tracking device has also included ensuring that the maximum quantity of solar energy consumption. Renewable energy might power four essential kitchen appliances, according to the idea of this project's design. During the day, the solar energy supplies load directly, and the rest of the energy is stored in a lead-acid battery. The battery supplies power during the night to execute the AC loads via an inverter. In MATLAB Simulink, the system configuration had displayed, and the outcome had exhibited graphically. This process represents a kitchen concept that is safe, cost-effective, and environmentally good for human health.

articleTitle: An Analytical Method to Determine the Maximum Wind Power Penetration Level
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Frequency stability in power system is ensured by means of inertia of synchronous generator. As there is renewable power generation in the grid, system inertia gets reduced. This reduction in inertia causes reduction in stability of frequency, especially in the case of a large contingency. So, we need to calculate effectively and accurately the maximum renewable power penetration level before a contingency occurs. This calculation of maximum renewable penetration level is a function of the level of contingency, the allowed maximum rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) and allowed minimum frequency nadir. In this paper, we use the Inverse Laplace Transformation of the full multi-machine system frequency response (MM-SFR) model of the IEEE 39-bus 10-machine New England system to find maximum renewable (wind) power penetration level (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$WPPL_{max}$</tex>) for an allowed minimum level of frequency nadir and at a fixed contingency level of 8.27%. Finally, we use DIgSILENT PowerFactory Software to simulate this power system for the same contingency level, and thus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$WPPL_{max}$</tex> is calculated to evaluate the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Distributed Energy Aggregations based on Cyber-Physical-Social Systems Modeling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: With the increased use of communications and control systems in the power distribution grid, and the ability of distributed energy resources to conform aggregations for wholesale power market participation, new modeling techniques are required to model the next generation of power systems comprehensively. Conventional power system modeling concerning physical systems no longer suffices to address the novel smart grid technologies and new business models for aggregations; more comprehensive approaches are required to jointly model the Cyber-Physical-Social Systems (CPSS) involved in the power sector. This paper proposed a framework to model distributed energy aggregations and their participation in the wholesale market based on CPSS modeling. The paper is a step forward to understand the mutual interdependence and coupling between the cyber, social, and physical systems to help future policymakers make decisions aligned to the interests of all the three proposed layers.

articleTitle: Time Controlled Power Supply Design for Magnetically Impelled Arc Butt Welding
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Magnetically Impelled Arc Butt (MIAB) Welding is a forge welding technique that is used to join ferrous pipes and tubes using high speed rotation of an arc as the heating source that softens the weld parts and a short duration upset force for forming the weld. Parametrical analysis conducted for experimental joining of carbon steel tubes of 21.5mm Outer Diameters (OD) and the thickness ranging between 1.5-2mm suggested the control of current in the two stages of this weld technique. This work attempts to simulate the control of power supply circuit using SIMULINK -MATLAB, so as to provide two current levels for the two stages of this weld technique. 3Phase to DC conversion circuit is used and the difference in current levels is brought about with the inclusion of time-controlled change in the circuit resistance. This study can be extended further by physical implementation of the proposed power system to verify the efficient control of the current levels in bringing out an effective weld.

articleTitle: Effects of channel length and oxide layer modulation on the performance of Ga2O3 MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Wide bandgap (WBG) based semiconductor devices are being widely adopted in power electronic applications, especially in power converters, for their excellent material properties in recent years. The material properties of Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and its possibility to power device performance are discussed. In this work, a Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> MOSFET structure is simulated using Silvaco TCAD. The effects of variation in channel length, oxide layer thickness, and material of oxide layer on the characteristics of the MOSFET are investigated. The shorter channel length results in higher drain current, low on-resistance, and high transconductance. The thicker the oxide layer, the higher the drain current is realized. It is also found that SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is more suitable than Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> in Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based MOSFET.

articleTitle: Variable Power Reaching Law-Sliding Mode Controllers for Partial Linearized SMIB Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: For synchronous generators (SGs), a variable power reaching law-sliding mode controller (VPRL-SMC) is proposed in this study to improve the performance of transient stability in a small power system. The theory of feedback linearizing controller (FBLC) and SMC are integrated in this work to construct the proposed excitation controller. Using the partial FBLC, the nonlinear model is first transformed into a linearized reduced-order model. The VPRL-SMC is then used to obtain the control input for the excitation system. As a result, the suggested excitation controller will be able to improve transient stability more quickly while also avoiding the need to measure the rotor angle because the speed deviation will be employed as an output. To ensure the system's overall stability, the control Lyapunov function theory is used. Finally, the MATLAB platform is used to put the proposed controller's theoretical notion into practice. The simulation result is compared to the existing controller to demonstrate the suggested controller's superiority.

articleTitle: Design of a Robust Integral Sliding Mode Controller Using the Continuous Function-Based Fast Power Reaching Law for DC-DC Boost Converters in Fuel Cells Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents a continuous function-based fast power reaching law-nonlinear robust integral sliding mode control scheme for regulating the output voltage of a DC-DC boost converter in applications of a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). An averaged mathematical model of the DC-DC boost converter is used for designing the proposed controller where the main control objective is tracking of the reference output voltage. To guarantee the nominal operation of the system under uncertainties, the bounded external disturbances are included with the model. The stability of the system while ensuring the desired tracking of the output voltage is proved using the theory of candidate Lyapunov functions. At last, the performance of the proposed controller is verified via the MATLAB/Simulink by varying the reference output voltage. For showing superiority, the performance of the proposed controller is also compared with the performance of a conventional sliding mode controller. Simulation results evident that the proposed controller is better than the conventional sliding mode controller in terms of settling time, overshoot, and steady-state tracking error.

articleTitle: Generating a Cost Effective Solar Study Lamp and Solar Home Solution using Android Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: More than half a billion children suffer from insufficient lighting, relying on dim, smoky, and hazardous kerosene-based lighting for their studies especially in rural area at night time. In this paper, a brighter, cleaner, secure and zero-marginal-cost light of solar lights has been modeled to rural learners that could enhance their learning outcomes. This paper consists of two primary components, where the first part is to produce a cost-effective solar lamp that offers 150 lux constant light about 5 to 7 hours. These solar lamps are likely to have a negligible impact on the achievement of education. The second primary aspect of the project is to create the solar home scheme where an Android phone application is constructed on the solar home scheme. This application will calculates the critical apps of solar home scheme that offers inverter selection, usage of battery and PV module the user needs in sequence and parallel data. The results performed a solar study lamp which gives minimum amount of lightening and the features of durability and efficiency and a solar home system SHS that calculates critical applications, known as solar calculator for the customer.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control of Hybrid Power System with Water Evaporation Algorithm Optimized PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Load frequency control (LFC) of thermal plant coordinated microgrid system is investigated in this paper. The unique control signal is provided for fuel cell (FC), aqua-electrolyzer(AE) and diesel generator (DG) of the microgrid along with thermal plant to minimize the frequency deviations of the hybrid power system during load, PV and wind power disturbances. This scheme enhances the frequency stability of the microgrid when it is interconnected with conventional plants. Water evaporation algorithm (WEO) is used in this paper to find the optimal parameter gains of the controller. Further, the impact of storage elements on LFC is also discussed to show the advantage of their presence in the hybrid power system.

articleTitle: Voltage Profile Improvement by using DGs in Power System Resilient Framework
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronic and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The infrastructure and network of the power systems are becoming bigger and more complex day by day. For this reason, it has been more difficult to maintain a steady uninterrupted power flow. To obtain a better solution, the identification of a critical node is one of the important considerations in a resilient power system. In this paper, the authors have made an attempt to find out the betweenness centrality and then after deployment of distributed generations (DG) into the critical node to improve the voltage profile in different types of outages conditions.
